sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the 1930 Long Beach Island atlas shows the south-western part of Beach Haven at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It runs from South West Avenue at the top, across South Bay Avenue at about the middle, to South Beach Avenue at the bottom, and from Norwood Avenue at the left to Marine Street at the right, with Berkeley Avenue and Ocean Street between them. The upper tier of blocks (numbered 82, 83 and 84) lies on the bay side of Bay Avenue and is almost entirely drawn empty, with only a few small dwellings near Norwood Avenue and the Beach Haven Yacht Club building at the top edge near Berkeley Avenue. A baseball field is lettered in block 84, where one large irregular structure is drawn beside Ocean Street. The lower blocks (123, 124 and 125) between South Bay and South Beach Avenues hold scattered frame dwellings with outbuildings, thickest in the left-hand block. A scale bar, a north arrow with a note about hot dock water and the Princeton library stamp appear in the margins, and the adjoining sheets 3, 6 and 11 are named at the edges. A dark wedge at the lower left corner is a scan edge.
notes: Today Ocean and Marine are Ocean Street and Marine Street.
The Beach Haven Yacht Club is lettered at the top edge near Berkeley Avenue.
Lettering read at overview resolution except where noted; small building labels may be misread.
Beach Haven south-west centre, 50 ft, one part: Norwood and Berkeley Avs, Ocean, Marine (Streets) between S. West, S. Bay and S. Beach Avs. Helper-configured.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the 1930 Long Beach Island atlas shows the centre of Beach Haven at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It covers the blocks between Marine Street on the left and Amber Street on the right, from South Delaware Avenue (with the corner of South West Avenue at the top left) across South Bay Avenue to South Beach Avenue at the bottom; Pearl and Coral Streets cross the sheet between them. The bay-side blocks north of Bay Avenue hold the town's commercial and service buildings: a large brick garage on Pearl Street and the yard of J. Willits Berry, lumber and coal, with storage sheds, a lumber shed and a row of brick buildings facing Bay Avenue near Amber Street. South of Bay Avenue the blocks are residential, with scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings, and the Corinthian Yacht Club stands near Marine Street and Beach Avenue. Large parts of the upper blocks are drawn empty. Water pipes with their sizes, hydrants and house numbers are marked along the streets; the block numbers (85 to 87, 126 to 128) follow the atlas key. Adjoining sheets 2, 4 and 7 are named at the margins.
notes: Pearl, Coral, Amber and Marine are now Pearl Street, Coral Street, Amber Street and Marine Street.
J. Willits Berry lumber and coal yard on Bay Avenue between Coral and Amber.
Lettering read at overview resolution.

Beach Haven centre, 50 ft to an inch, north to the upper right (rotation about +61.5). Marine, Pearl, Coral, Amber (Streets) between S. Delaware Av, S. Bay Av and S. Beach Av; J. Willits Berry lumber yard, Corinthian Yacht Club. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 of the 1930 Long Beach Island atlas shows the middle of Beach Haven, around Bay Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It covers the area between Amber Street on the left and 2nd Street on the right, from Delaware Avenue at the top to Beach Avenue at the bottom, with the street lettered South and Center Street between. Bay Avenue crosses the middle and the Long Beach Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) runs diagonally through the upper blocks. The bay-side blocks hold the town's utilities and trades: the waterworks reservoir, built in 1929 with a capacity of 580,000 gallons, the Department of Highways garage, the fire station and a pumping and generating plant with storage cisterns, near Amber Street; the Beach Haven Ice and Cold Storage Company and a fish store in the middle; and, near Center Street, the lumber yard of Firman H. Cranmer, a coal yard, an auto sales and repair shop and the New Colonial motion picture theatre. South of Bay Avenue are residential blocks 129, 130 and 131 with a garage, an auto repair shop, the Beach Haven Hotel, the Magnolia and the Ocean House. Water pipes, hydrants and house numbers are marked along the streets.
notes: The street printed South is Engleside Avenue today; Center is Centre Street and Dock is Dock Road.
The Long Beach Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) right of way crosses the upper blocks and is no longer a running line.
The waterworks reservoir is lettered as built in 1929.
The abbreviations on this sheet were checked on full-resolution crops of the left and right bay-side blocks; the lower blocks were read at overview resolution.

Beach Haven centre, 50 ft, one part: Amber, South (Engleside Avenue), Center (Centre Street), Dock (Dock Road), 2nd St between S./N. Delaware, Bay and Beach Avs; commercial core. Helper-configured; street_widths 100 for Centre and Engleside.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the 1930 Long Beach Island atlas shows the northern end of the central Beach Haven blocks at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It lies between 2nd Street at the left and 5th Street at the right, from North Delaware Avenue at the top across Railroad Avenue and North Bay Avenue to North Beach Avenue at the bottom, with 3rd and 4th Streets between. The Long Beach Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses the upper blocks and the Beach Haven railroad station, marked with a ticket office, stands beside the tracks in block 93. Blocks 92, 94 and 95 along Railroad Avenue and Bay Avenue hold a line of shops, a plumbing shop, a storage building and a few small outbuildings at the left, with other blocks drawn empty. South of Bay Avenue, blocks 132, 133 and 134 contain scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings, and the Colonial motion picture theatre stands in block 133. Street widths and water pipes are marked, and adjoining sheets 4, 9 and 12 are named at the margins.
notes: Beach Haven railroad station is drawn beside the Long Beach Railroad tracks near 3rd Street.
North Beach Avenue is Beach Avenue today.
Lettering read at overview resolution except where noted; small building labels may be misread.
Beach Haven north, 50 ft, one part: 2nd to 5th St, N. Delaware, Railroad, N. Bay, N. Beach Avs; L.B.R.R. Beach Haven depot. Helper-configured.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 of the 1930 Long Beach Island atlas shows the south-western oceanfront blocks of Beach Haven at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It lies between Norwood Avenue and Marine Street, with Berkeley Avenue and Ocean between, and runs from South Beach Avenue at the top across South Atlantic Avenue to the beach, the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean at the bottom. The blocks between South Beach and South Atlantic Avenues (161, 162 and 163) hold scattered frame dwellings with outbuildings, with a few larger houses at the right; one pink structure stands in block 162. The ocean-side blocks (199, 200 and 201) are drawn empty, with the Boardwalk shown as a pair of dashed lines near the shore and a pier or walk at the left. The shore line and the surf are tinted blue, and a north arrow and the Princeton library stamp appear in the lower margin. Sheet 2 lies above and sheets 7 and 10 are named at the edges.
notes: Ocean and Marine are Ocean Street and Marine Street today.
The Boardwalk lies along the shore at the foot of the ocean-side blocks.
Lettering read at overview resolution except where noted; small building labels may be misread.
Beach Haven oceanfront, 50 ft, one part: Norwood, Berkeley, Ocean, Marine between S. Beach and S. Atlantic Avs. Helper-configured.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 of the 1930 Long Beach Island atlas shows the central oceanfront of Beach Haven at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It lies between Marine and Amber, with Pearl and Coral between, and runs from South Beach Avenue at the top across South Atlantic Avenue to the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean at the bottom. The large Hotel Baldwin occupies most of block 164 at the left, with its kitchen, dining room, laundry, help quarters and ice house; a lettered note describes its construction and water supply. The Hotel Baldwin bath houses and a shed stand on the beach side in block 202. The middle block 165 holds small cottages and outbuildings in two rows, and block 166 at the right holds frame dwellings and a hospital lettered as the Babies Hospital of Philadelphia. The ocean-side blocks 203 and 204 are otherwise empty, and the Boardwalk runs across the lower part of the sheet with a small stand beside it. The surf line is tinted blue. A north arrow is at lower left and the Princeton library stamp at lower right.
notes: Pearl, Coral, Amber and Marine are Pearl Street, Coral Street, Amber Street and Marine Street today.
Hotel Baldwin and its bath houses are lettered on the sheet.
Lettering read at overview resolution except where noted; small building labels may be misread.
Beach Haven oceanfront, 50 ft, one part: Marine, Pearl, Coral, Amber between S. Beach and S. Atlantic Avs; Hotel Baldwin, Babies' Hospital. Helper-configured.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 of the 1930 Long Beach Island atlas shows the eastern oceanfront of Beach Haven at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It lies between Amber at the left and 2nd Street at the right, with the street lettered South and Center between, and runs from South and North Beach Avenues at the top across South and North Atlantic Avenues to the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean at the bottom. The Engleside Hotel, closed in winter, fills most of block 167 at the left with a long main building; block 168 holds the Episcopal church, The St. Rita and frame dwellings, and block 169 holds the Kynette M.E. Church, the public library and more dwellings. The ocean-side blocks (205, 206 and 207) are mostly empty apart from the Engleside Hotel bath houses and a pavilion on the Boardwalk. The shore is tinted blue and a north arrow and scale bar are in the lower margin.
notes: The street printed South is Engleside Avenue today and Center is Centre Street.
The church names are read at overview resolution and may be imperfect.
Lettering read at overview resolution except where noted; small building labels may be misread.
Beach Haven oceanfront, 50 ft, one part: Amber, South, Center, 2nd St between Beach and Atlantic Avs; Engleside Hotel. Helper-configured.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the northern end of the Beach Haven built-up area at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It runs from North Beach Avenue near the top edge to North Atlantic Avenue about two thirds of the way down, and continues below that as platted blocks to the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean along the bottom edge. The cross streets are 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets, running down the sheet; the neighbouring sheets are numbered 5, 8, 12 and 13 in the corners. The upper blocks hold scattered dwellings, a pink-coloured Public Library near 2nd and 3rd Streets, a church with a long frontage on a block between 3rd and 4th Streets, and several outbuildings. Between 4th and 5th Streets the block is nearly empty apart from a cluster of dwellings at its right end. South of North Atlantic Avenue the blocks are numbered 208, 209 and 210 and are almost bare, with a few houses near 2nd Street and two stores or sheds near the Boardwalk. The shoreline is drawn as a line with a tinted strip, and the Boardwalk is shown as a pair of dashed lines along the beach. Water pipes and hydrants are marked on the avenues. The title cartouche and compass rose stand at the right.
notes: North Beach Avenue is now Beach Avenue; North Atlantic Avenue keeps its name. The cross streets are today 2nd to 5th Street.
Fitted from 8 automatic junctions of the cross streets with Beach and North Atlantic Avenues (RMSE 0.39 m).
Beach Haven north oceanfront, 50 ft, one part: 2nd to 5th St between N. Beach and N. Atlantic Avs; public library, church, boardwalk. Helper-configured.

sheet-10-1.description: Main part of sheet 10: the south end of Beach Haven at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right. It runs from Nelson Avenue at the left edge to Iroquois Avenue at the right edge, and from South Pennsylvania Avenue near Liberty Thoroughfare on the bay side, across South West Avenue (marked not open), South Bay Avenue and South Beach Avenue, to South Atlantic Avenue and the beach, with the Atlantic Ocean noted beyond. The cross streets are Nelson, Merivale, Leeward, Kentford, Jefferis, Stratford, Pelham, Liberty and Iroquois Avenues. The area is almost entirely platted but unbuilt in 1930: long blocks divided into numbered 50 ft lots (blocks 66 to 73, 107 to 114, 145 to 152, 183 to 190), with only a few dwellings near Bay Avenue and at the Iroquois end. Water pipes run along Bay Avenue and some cross streets. The top left of the sheet is taken up by an inset of the Beach Haven bay front (part 2), outlined by a heavy line, so the bay-side blocks between Leeward and Jefferis Avenues are not shown here. Ocean-side streets south of Liberty Avenue have since been lost or replatted.
notes: Printed JEFFERIS; the modern street is Jeffries Avenue.
South West Avenue is marked 'not open'.

South Beach Avenue and South Atlantic Avenue south of Liberty Avenue are no longer in the modern street network; South Pennsylvania and South West Avenues lie 4 to 13 m off their 1930 line, so only Bay Avenue, Beach Avenue (Liberty) and West Avenue junctions were used.

Two parts, 100 ft. Part 1 (main): south Beach Haven, Nelson to Iroquois Avs (JEFFERIS = Jeffries Avenue), S. Pennsylvania/S. West (not open)/S. Bay/S. Beach/S. Atlantic Avs; nearly all platted, empty lots. Part 2: inset outlined by a heavy line in the upper left, the Beach Haven bay front north of Delaware Av (Ambler = Amber Street, South = Engleside Avenue, Center = Centre Street, Dock = Dock Road, 2nd St); hotel, club, wharves. S. West and S. Pennsylvania Avs in part 1 are 4 to 13 m off their modern line; Nelson and Iroquois/S. Beach misdetected at the sheet edges.

sheet-10-2.description: Inset on sheet 10, outlined by a heavy line in the upper left of the sheet: the bay front of Beach Haven north of Delaware Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the same orientation as the main map (north toward the upper right). It shows the blocks from Ambler (Amber Street) at the left edge, through the 100 ft street lettered South, Center and Dock, to 2nd Street, between the curving shore of Little Egg Harbor Bay with South and North West Avenue at the top, South and North Pennsylvania Avenue in the middle and North and South Delaware Avenue along the bottom. The western blocks (54, 55, 61) are platted lots with only a few dwellings; the blocks along Center Street and Dock are built up with dwellings, a garage for twelve cars near the boat ramp, and on the shore at Dock a hotel, a club and wharves with boat houses. A boat ramp, platforms and water pipes are drawn along the bay. The inset was placed on this sheet for room; on the ground it lies north of sheets 3 and 4.
notes: Printed AMBLER; the index and modern map have Amber Street.
The street lettered SOUTH between Ambler and Center is now Engleside Avenue (by position).
Center is now Centre Street; Dock is Dock Road.

Two parts, 100 ft. Part 1 (main): south Beach Haven, Nelson to Iroquois Avs (JEFFERIS = Jeffries Avenue), S. Pennsylvania/S. West (not open)/S. Bay/S. Beach/S. Atlantic Avs; nearly all platted, empty lots. Part 2: inset outlined by a heavy line in the upper left, the Beach Haven bay front north of Delaware Av (Ambler = Amber Street, South = Engleside Avenue, Center = Centre Street, Dock = Dock Road, 2nd St); hotel, club, wharves. S. West and S. Pennsylvania Avs in part 1 are 4 to 13 m off their modern line; Nelson and Iroquois/S. Beach misdetected at the sheet edges.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows the southern part of Beach Haven at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. The top is the bay side: Mordecai Island and the water called Liberty Thoroughfare, with a bulkhead line and narrow bayfront lots numbered 38 to 45 along the shore. Four long bands of blocks run across the sheet, divided by S. West, S. Bay, S. Beach and S. Atlantic Avenues, and crossed by the avenues Holyoak, Glendola, Fairview, Essex, Dolphin, Chatsworth, Belvoir and Norwood, with Iroquois Avenue at the left edge. Several of these are marked 60 feet wide. Almost every block is platted into numbered lots, but only a few have buildings: dwellings cluster in the right half between S. Bay and S. Atlantic Avenues near Chatsworth, Belvoir and Norwood Avenues, and along the bayfront. The bottom edge reaches the Atlantic Ocean, with the Boardwalk at the lower right. Blocks are numbered from 38 to 198. A compass rose stands at the upper left and the cartouche at the top right; the scale bar and Princeton library stamp are at the foot.
notes: S. West, S. Bay, S. Beach and S. Atlantic Avenues are now South West Avenue, South Bay Avenue, South Beach Avenue and South Atlantic Avenue; Holyoak Avenue is Holyoke Avenue today.
Avenue junctions on this sheet carry 3 to 4 m residuals in the fit (Essex, Norwood, Holyoak), probably because the modern avenue centrelines are displaced from the 1930 drawing.
South Beach Haven, 100 ft, one part: Iroquois/Holyoak to Norwood Avs between S. West and S. Atlantic Avs; Mordecai Island and Liberty Thoroughfare at top. Helper-configured; Holyoak = Holyoke Avenue.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows North Beach Haven at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right, from the bay shore to the ocean. At the top is Little Egg Harbor Bay with the Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) running across above the first row of blocks, and at the upper right the boat yard and buildings of Strickland Bros. on the bay shore. Below the railroad, rows of blocks are bounded by Railroad Avenue and North Bay Avenue, then North Beach Avenue, North Atlantic Avenue and Seaside Avenue at the foot, with the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean beyond. The cross streets, from left to right, are 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, Taylor Avenue, 9th, 10th, 11th and 12th Streets; Taylor Avenue is marked 100 feet wide and 9th Street 60 feet wide. Most blocks are platted lots with few buildings. Dwellings are concentrated at the left edge near 5th Street, along North Beach Avenue near 6th and 8th Streets, and in the cluster of buildings by the boat yard at the right. The Beach Haven School House stands in the block between North Bay and North Beach Avenues at 7th Street. Water pipes and hydrants are marked on the avenues. North Delaware Avenue appears at the upper left.
notes: North Bay Avenue, North Beach Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue are now North Bay Avenue, Beach Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue; Atlantic Avenue continues from 12th Street.
8th Street to 11th Street and Taylor Avenue lie 3 to 18 m from the 1930 drawing in the modern data; 5th, 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th Streets and Taylor Avenue were left out of the fit.
Neighbouring sheet numbers 5, 9 and 13 are printed at the edges.

North Beach Haven, 100 ft, one part: 5th to 12th St, Taylor Av, N. Delaware, Railroad, N. Bay, N. Beach, N. Atlantic Avs; railroad and Strickland Bros. boat yard. 9th, 10th St and Taylor Av are 14 to 18 m off their modern lines and 8th and 11th St 4 to 5 m: left out; placed from 6th, 7th and 12th St only.

sheet-13-1.description: Left part of sheet 13: North Beach Haven at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right, separated from the right part by a heavy vertical line. It runs from the Beach Haven borough line (Long Beach Township line) at the left edge across 13th, 14th, 15th and 16th Streets to 17th Street, and from Eagleswood Avenue and the shore of Little Egg Harbor Bay at the top, across Waverly Avenue, the Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) right of way, North Bay Avenue, North Beach Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue, to Seaside Avenue at the bottom by the Atlantic Ocean. The bay-side blocks are platted lots, nearly empty; a station stands by the railroad. Dwellings cluster between North Bay and North Atlantic Avenues near 13th and 14th Streets, where The Waverly and the Hotel Breakers are drawn. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along the avenues.
notes: 13th to 17th Streets are now West and East 13th to 17th Street either side of North Bay Avenue; North Beach Avenue is Beach Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue is Atlantic Avenue.
The North Bay Avenue / 17th Street junction lies on the dividing line and was rejected (8 m).
Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) right of way drawn between Waverly and North Bay Avenues.

Two parts, 100 ft, divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1: North Beach Haven, 13th to 17th St, Eagleswood/Waverly/N. Bay/N. Beach/N. Atlantic/Seaside Avs, L.B.R.R.; Beach Haven borough line at the left edge. Part 2: Spray Beach, 21st to 24th St (18th-20th not on this sheet), N. Bay/N. Beach/N. Atlantic Av, The Strand; Spray Beach Hotel and Yacht Club. Modern: West/East Nth Street, Beach Avenue, Atlantic Avenue.

sheet-13-2.description: Right part of sheet 13: Spray Beach at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right, separated from North Beach Haven (part 1) by a heavy line; streets 18th to 20th are not shown between the two parts. It covers 21st to 24th Streets from the shore of Little Egg Harbor Bay, with the Long Beach Railroad and the Spray Beach Yacht Club and its plank walk, across North Bay Avenue, North Beach Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue to The Strand and the beach, with Seaside Avenue lettered at the lower left. Development is concentrated between North Beach and North Atlantic Avenues and along 23rd Street: dwellings, apartments, a pump house, and the Spray Beach Hotel with a row of bath houses on The Strand. A garage and fire bell stand at North Bay Avenue and 23rd Street. The bay-side blocks are mostly open.
notes: 21st to 24th Streets are now East 21st to 24th Street; North Beach Avenue is Beach Avenue, North Atlantic Avenue is Atlantic Avenue.
Spray Beach Hotel and Spray Beach Yacht Club.

Two parts, 100 ft, divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1: North Beach Haven, 13th to 17th St, Eagleswood/Waverly/N. Bay/N. Beach/N. Atlantic/Seaside Avs, L.B.R.R.; Beach Haven borough line at the left edge. Part 2: Spray Beach, 21st to 24th St (18th-20th not on this sheet), N. Bay/N. Beach/N. Atlantic Av, The Strand; Spray Beach Hotel and Yacht Club. Modern: West/East Nth Street, Beach Avenue, Atlantic Avenue.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows Spray Beach and the subdivisions of Beach Haven Gardens and Beach Haven Bay Vista at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. The lower and larger part is a grid between North Bay Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean, with North Beach Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue crossing it, and The Strand running along the beach above the shore. The cross streets from left to right are 24th to 32nd Streets. The blocks carry numbers and letters and are platted into narrow lots, mostly empty, with houses scattered along North Beach Avenue and in the blocks between 24th and 30th Streets. At the top the Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) crosses on the diagonal, beside Baltic Avenue. North of Baltic Avenue is the Beach Haven Bay Vista subdivision, with blocks lettered A to E between 28th and 32nd Streets and Pacific Avenue at the top, edged by the winding shore of Little Egg Harbor Bay, which is drawn with an irregular tidal creek. A compass rose stands at the upper left, the cartouche at the top right and the scale bar at the lower left.
notes: North Beach Avenue and North Atlantic Avenue are now Beach Avenue and Atlantic Avenue; North Bay Avenue becomes Long Beach Boulevard from 29th Street east. The cross streets are East 24th to East 30th Street and South 31st and 32nd Street today.
Baltic Avenue junctions fit within about 1 to 2 m of the street grid and were used, which gives control in the Bay Vista area at the top.
Neighbouring sheets 13 and 15 are printed at the left and right edges.
Spray Beach, Beach Haven Gardens and Bay Vista, 100 ft, one part: 24th to 32nd St, Pacific, Baltic, N. Bay, N. Beach, N. Atlantic Avs, The Strand. Helper-configured.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows the Beach Haven Gardens, Beach Haven Bay Vista and Beach Haven Terrace subdivisions at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. The left strip, between Little Egg Harbor Bay and the ocean, has the lettered and numbered blocks of Bay Vista at the top, running down to Baltic Avenue, and the numbered blocks of Beach Haven Gardens below the Long Beach Railroad, with 32nd, 33rd and 34th Streets, North Beach Avenue, North Atlantic Avenue and The Strand. Garden Harbor, a narrow inlet, is drawn at the upper left. The right two thirds shows the avenues Delaware, Maryland, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Indiana and Ohio running from Pacific Avenue to the ocean and crossed by Baltic Avenue, North Bay Avenue and Atlantic Avenue, in blocks numbered 502 to 525 and laid out in long narrow lots. Houses stand along the avenues between North Bay and Atlantic Avenues, and the U.S. Coast Guard Long Beach Station and the Victoria Apartments are drawn near the ocean end of Pennsylvania and Maryland Avenues. The Long Beach Water Co. is marked beside Baltic Avenue. The railroad crosses the sheet above North Bay Avenue.
notes: The avenues are now numbered streets with the old names appended: Delaware Avenue is East 133rd Street Delaware Avenue, Maryland 132nd, Pennsylvania 131rd, New Jersey 130th, Indiana 129th and Ohio 128th Street; the boulevard at North Bay Avenue is Long Beach Boulevard.
Baltic Avenue junctions are 3 to 6 m from the drawing and were left out, so the upper half of the sheet is controlled only through the street grid below it.
New Jersey and Indiana Avenues at Long Beach Boulevard were rejected (21 to 23 m); the right side of the sheet has no control from there upwards.

Beach Haven Gardens, Bay Vista and Terrace, 100 ft, one part: 32nd to 34th St and Delaware to Ohio Avs (now East 128th to 133rd Street ... Avenue), U.S. Coast Guard station. Baltic Av displaced 3 to 6 m, left out; the bay-side upper half has no control.

sheet-16-1.description: Lower part of sheet 16, below the heavy dividing line: Brant Beach at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It runs from the Bayview Avenue frontage along the dividing line at the top, across a double line of the Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.), to Bay Avenue and then to Ocean Boulevard and the beach blocks at the foot. The avenues Sigsbee, Dupont, Goldsborough, Paulding, Farragut, Stanton, Kimberly, Harmonyo and Selfridge cross the sheet from left to right. Most blocks are lettered or numbered subdivision lots. Houses are concentrated in the band between Bay Avenue and Ocean Boulevard, especially near Goldsborough, Paulding and Farragut Avenues, and a camp, with its own outbuildings, stands at the lower right. A bay-side tract at the top of the part, below Bayview Avenue, contains a pump house and an elevated tank and blocks lettered I to L. The words Brant Beach are lettered across the middle. Block lines are mostly empty at the lower left, where beach lots are marked in sections. The scale bar and the library stamp are at the foot.
notes: The avenues are now numbered streets with the old names appended, East and West 57th (Selfridge) to 65th (Sigsbee) Street; Bay Avenue is Long Beach Boulevard.
Harmonyo is printed so; the modern name is Harmony Avenue.
Part 3 of the sheet (the bay-side area with Barnegat Avenue at the upper right, outside the heavy line) is not georeferenced.

Three parts, 100 ft, divided by an L-shaped heavy line. Part 1: Brant Beach, Sigsbee to Selfridge Avs (now East 57th to 65th Street ... Avenue), Bay Av, Bayview Av, Ocean Blvd. Part 2: Beach Haven Crest, Roberts to Lavenia Avs (75th to 79th), Bay Av, Ocean Av, Ocean Blvd. Part 3 (upper right, bay side, Barnegat Av, blocks P, O, B): not configured.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: bay-side blocks P, O and B on Barnegat Avenue and a tidal creek, right of the heavy line (only one lettered street (Barnegat Av), cross streets unlettered; including it with part 1 raised the RMSE from 0.85 to 6.1 m; needs parcel corners or a carried block corner from part 1).

sheet-16-2.description: Upper left part of sheet 16, inside the heavy dividing line: Beach Haven Crest at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. Bay Avenue runs across near the top, below the Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) and a row of blocks numbered 15 to 21; Ocean Avenue crosses below the middle, and Ocean Boulevard runs along the heavy dividing line at the foot, with the Atlantic Ocean beyond. The avenues, from left to right, are Roberts, Winifred, Jeannette, Hobart, Culver and Lavenia. The blocks are numbered 1 to 14 and are platted into narrow lots. Houses fill the blocks between Bay Avenue and Ocean Avenue, with the Hotel Crest and several outbuildings in block 11, and a fish packing building by the railroad at the upper right. The blocks between Ocean Avenue and Ocean Boulevard are nearly empty. The title Beach Haven Crest is lettered across the top. The heavy line forms the lower and right edge of the part; below and to the right are the Brant Beach part and the Barnegat Avenue area.
notes: The avenues are now numbered streets with the old names appended, East and West 75th (Lavenia) to 79th (Winifred) Street; Roberts Avenue has no match in the modern data. Bay Avenue is Long Beach Boulevard and the 1930 Ocean Avenue is today Ocean Boulevard; the 1930 Ocean Boulevard no longer exists.
Fitted from 10 automatic junctions (RMSE 0.47 m).

Three parts, 100 ft, divided by an L-shaped heavy line. Part 1: Brant Beach, Sigsbee to Selfridge Avs (now East 57th to 65th Street ... Avenue), Bay Av, Bayview Av, Ocean Blvd. Part 2: Beach Haven Crest, Roberts to Lavenia Avs (75th to 79th), Bay Av, Ocean Av, Ocean Blvd. Part 3 (upper right, bay side, Barnegat Av, blocks P, O, B): not configured.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: bay-side blocks P, O and B on Barnegat Avenue and a tidal creek, right of the heavy line (only one lettered street (Barnegat Av), cross streets unlettered; including it with part 1 raised the RMSE from 0.85 to 6.1 m; needs parcel corners or a carried block corner from part 1).

sheet-17-1.description: Main map of sheet 17, covering the Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington end of the island from 31st Street at the left edge to 27th Street and Ship Bottom Avenue at the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The upper left corner is cut out by the Brant Beach inset (part 2), outlined by a heavy line, and the bay shore with a stretch of water lies below it. Central Avenue runs along the top, with a row of bay-side blocks of platted lots and a few dwellings near 28th and 27th Streets. The Long Beach Railroad crosses the sheet, then Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard, which carries a long block-lined frontage on its ocean side. Below it the ocean-side blocks, divided into numbered narrow lots (many empty, some with dwellings between 29th and 27th Streets), run down to Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean at the bottom. A garage and repair shop (blue) and a tile-roofed building stand on the boulevard near 27th Street. Union Avenue crosses at the right, below which are a few dwellings near Ship Bottom Avenue. At the left edge a dash-dot line marks the limit between Long Beach Township and the Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington borough along 31st Street. Water pipes are lettered along the streets, and there is a compass rose in the bay-shore area and the title oval at the top right.
notes: Streets north-west of the boulevard are lettered 'St. N.W.'; the modern names are West 27th and West 28th Street (West 29th to 31st Street are not in the modern network), and East 27th to East 31st Street on the ocean side.

The boulevard junctions here sit about 3 to 4 m from the modern nodes while the Central Avenue and Union Avenue junctions agree; the sheet's fitted scale is about 1.5 percent below the neighbouring sheets.
East 31st Street / Long Beach Boulevard at the left edge was left out (a one-edged street at the sheet limit, 7 m off).
The scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch.
Bay-side stretches of the numbered streets are lettered "St. N.W." (now West Nth Street), the ocean-side stretches "St." (now East Nth Street).

Two parts, 50 ft (scale bar 50, not 100). Part 1: Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington, Ship Bottom Av to 31st St, Central, Union, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av. Part 2: inset in the upper left, Brant Beach at 34th and 35th St on Bay Av (movie theatre and apartments), anchored on two boulevard junctions: low confidence.

sheet-17-2.description: Inset at the upper left of sheet 17, outlined by heavy lines on its right and lower sides, headed 'Brant Beach' and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the upper right. It shows two blocks wide of the Brant Beach end of Bay Avenue, the street along the top of the inset, between 35th Street on the left and 34th Street on the right, and the shore of the bay below. The upper row of blocks is a single large building, a movie theatre with apartments and offices in a block drawn in blue, with 'Movies', 'Apartments' and an entrance marked on it and steam heat, electric light and chemical extinguishers noted. Below it a second row of blocks (41, 43 and 45) is platted with lots and carries no buildings. The bay and its curved shore with an irregular marsh edge fill the lower left, where a compass rose is drawn. The inset was placed on sheet 17 for room: on the ground Brant Beach lies to the south-west of the main part of the sheet, and the inset is not at the same location. Street widths of 50 and 100 feet are lettered at the edges of the blocks and along the boundary line.
notes: Bay Avenue on the inset is the modern Long Beach Boulevard; the junctions with 35th and 34th Streets (modern East 35th and East 34th Street) are the only control and lie 60 m apart.
The centre of Bay Avenue is only partly drawn (one edge), so its position across the street is uncertain by several metres.
The scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch.

Two parts, 50 ft (scale bar 50, not 100). Part 1: Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington, Ship Bottom Av to 31st St, Central, Union, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av. Part 2: inset in the upper left, Brant Beach at 34th and 35th St on Bay Av (movie theatre and apartments), anchored on two boulevard junctions: low confidence.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington from Ship Bottom Avenue at the left edge to 23rd Street at the right edge, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Central Avenue runs along the top, below which the bay-side blocks (26, 28, 31) are mostly platted lots with a scatter of dwellings and a row of nine paired houses on 26th Street. The Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) crosses the sheet below them and a small passenger station for Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington stands beside the tracks at the right. Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard follows, then the ocean-side blocks (25, 29, 30) running down to Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean. The built-up part is along the boulevard: a large garage for thirty cars (blue) at 26th Street, a post office, the Conrad Bros. lumber and building material yard with its sheds and lumber piles near 24th and 23rd Streets, and a U.S. Coast Guard station beside Union Avenue at the left. Camp Dune by the Sea stands near the beach at 26th Street. Further down the lots are empty, laid out in long narrow rows. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inch size are lettered along the streets. A compass rose lies right of centre, and the title oval and a 'Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington' heading are at the top right.
notes: Streets north-west of the boulevard are lettered 'St. N.W.'; the modern names are West 23rd to West 26th Street, with East 23rd to East 26th Street south-east of Long Beach Boulevard.
Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard is the modern Long Beach Boulevard; Ship Bottom Avenue and Union Avenue are the modern Ship Bottom Avenue and Union Avenue.
The junctions at Ship Bottom Avenue and Union Avenue at the left edge were not detected and are not control points.
The scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch.
Bay-side stretches of the numbered streets are lettered "St. N.W." (now West Nth Street), the ocean-side stretches "St." (now East Nth Street).

Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington, 50 ft, one part: Ship Bottom Av to 23rd St (St. N.W. on the bay side), Central, Union, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av; L.B.R.R. station, Conrad Bros. lumber. Helper-configured.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 shows Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington from 23rd Street at the left edge to 19th Street at the right edge, at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Central Avenue runs along the top, with a row of bay-side blocks (36, 39, 44, 47) below it; the right-hand blocks are built up with small dwellings facing Penna Avenue. Below Penna Avenue the Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) right of way crosses the sheet, with a freight station beside the tracks at the far left. Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard is drawn in two offset stretches: west of 22nd Street it lies higher on the sheet, and east of it the boulevard steps down about 20 metres, with a blank margin where its edges are not drawn. The ocean-side blocks (37, 38, 45, 46) run down to Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean at the bottom. Dwellings are concentrated along the boulevard between 21st and 19th Streets, where a post office, a garage for fifteen cars (blue) and a chapel stand, and thin out towards the beach, where the lots are still empty. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inch size are lettered along the streets. A compass rose is placed in the blank area right of the railroad, and the title oval at top right. Matching sheet numbers 18 and 20 are printed at the left and right edges.
notes: The streets north-west of the boulevard are lettered 'St. N.W.'; the modern names are West 19th to West 23rd Street, and East 19th to East 22nd Street on the ocean side.

The drawn boulevard east of 22nd Street lies on the modern East-numbered Long Beach Boulevard nodes about 20 m from the West-numbered ones, so the East-only nodes were used there and the others left out.
The junctions of the boulevard with 21st and 20th Streets are hand-picked from the street and pipe centre lines because the boulevard edges are not drawn.
The scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch.
Bay-side stretches of the numbered streets are lettered "St. N.W." (now West Nth Street), the ocean-side stretches "St." (now East Nth Street).

Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington, 50 ft, one part: 23rd to 19th St, Central, Penna Av, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av. The modern boulevard jogs about 20 m at 22nd St (West/East nodes excluded by coordinates); two hand-picked boulevard junctions.

sheet-20-1.description: Left part of sheet 20, separated from the right part by a heavy vertical line, showing the Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington section from 19th Street at the left edge to 17th Street at the right, at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Central Avenue runs along the top. Below it, at the left, a row of nine small dwellings faces Penna Avenue, and beside 18th and 17th Streets stands the Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington Water Works, with a pump house (pink) and an iron stand pipe 115 feet high of 152,000 gallons capacity. The Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) crosses the middle of the sheet. Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard follows; it is drawn in two offset stretches, lower on the sheet west of 18th Street and higher east of it, with the Beach Arlington Fire Co. No. 1 house at the left. Ocean-side blocks 546, 547 and 548 run down to Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean, with a scale bar at the bottom left. Dwellings are concentrated along 18th and 17th Streets between the boulevard and the beach, while the eastern block (548) and the beach ends of the streets remain empty. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inch size are lettered along the streets. A compass rose lies in the rail corridor, and sheet number 20 is printed at the top.
notes: Streets north-west of the boulevard are lettered 'St. N.W.'; the modern names are West 17th to West 19th Street, with East 17th to East 19th Street south-east of Long Beach Boulevard.
West of 18th Street the drawn boulevard matches the East-numbered modern nodes; east of it the combined West/East nodes. The offset nodes were left out.
The scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch.
Bay-side stretches of the numbered streets are lettered "St. N.W." (now West Nth Street), the ocean-side stretches "St." (now East Nth Street).

Two parts, 50 ft, divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1: Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington, 19th to 17th St, Central, Penna, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av; water works, fire company. Part 2: separate block between Barnegat and Central Avs at 18th and 17th St.

sheet-20-2.description: Right part of sheet 20, to the right of a heavy vertical line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a north arrow pointing to the upper right. It is a separate block of the bay side of Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington, placed beside the main part for room: it runs from Barnegat Avenue along the top to Central Avenue along the bottom, with 18th Street at the left, cut off by the heavy line, and 17th Street to the right of it; the part continues to the right edge with the beginning of a further block and street. The blocks between Barnegat and Central Avenues are long, narrow platted lots numbered in the 200s (for example 291, 282, 276, 269, 255, 247, 244, 237, 216, 209, 202), with only a handful of dwellings, mostly in the middle of the block between 18th and 17th Streets and, in a cluster of five or six, close to Central Avenue at the lower left, where lot numbers 1703 to 1715 are written. Blocks are numbered 8 and 9. A 6 inch water pipe runs beside 17th Street near the bottom. The caption 'Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington' and the title oval are at the top, and sheet number 20 is printed at the upper right and at the foot of the part.
notes: The streets are the modern West 18th and West 17th Street between Barnegat Avenue and Central Avenue; on the ground this block lies bayward (north-west) of the left part of the sheet.
18th Street is cut by the heavy line, so its junctions are measured from one edge; the part has four control points.
The scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch.

Two parts, 50 ft, divided by a heavy vertical line. Part 1: Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington, 19th to 17th St, Central, Penna, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av; water works, fire company. Part 2: separate block between Barnegat and Central Avs at 18th and 17th St.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 of the Long Beach Island atlas covers the Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington section from 15th Street on the left to 12th Street on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Central Avenue runs along the top edge. Below it lie four blocks of platted but almost empty lots (blocks 542 to 545) on the bay side, with only six or seven dwellings near 14th and 13th Streets. A broad strip carrying the Long Beach Railroad (P.R.R.) separates them from Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard, which crosses the sheet at about one third of its height; the tracks curve off to the upper right near 13th Street. South of the boulevard the ocean-side blocks (549 to 553) run down to Ocean Avenue, lettered 'not opened', with the Atlantic Ocean at the foot. These blocks are divided into narrow numbered lots and the dwellings are scattered, most of them between 15th and 13th Streets, with a few near the beach end of 13th and 12th Streets. Water pipes of 4 and 10 inch size are marked along the streets, and hydrants and a telephone or fire call box are shown. A compass rose sits at the left, the title oval and the words 'Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington' at the top right, and the left and right edges carry 'No exposure' notes where adjoining sheets continue.
notes: The streets north-west of the boulevard are lettered 'St. N.W.' on the sheet; the modern names are West 12th to West 15th Street, and East 12th to East 15th Street south-east of Long Beach Boulevard.
Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard is the modern Long Beach Boulevard; Ocean Avenue (not opened) is not in the modern street network.
The scale bar reads 50 ft to one inch, although the atlas-wide note gives 100 ft for the later sheets; the fit gives about 8.0 px/ft, which agrees with 50 ft.
Bay-side stretches of the numbered streets are lettered "St. N.W." (now West Nth Street), the ocean-side stretches "St." (now East Nth Street).
Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington, 50 ft, one part: 15th to 12th St, Central, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av. Helper-configured.

sheet-22-1.description: Top part of sheet 22, separated from the lower strips by a heavy line: the boundary between Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington and Surf City at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right. It runs from 6th Avenue at the left through 5th and 4th Avenues to 3rd Avenue (South 3rd Street), where the borough limits run down the street, then South 2nd and South 1st Streets, Division Avenue and North 1st Street. Across the island it reaches from Central Avenue at the top edge and Drexel Road, past a diagonal right of way, across Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard to Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean. Most blocks are platted lots with few buildings; dwellings stand along Bay Avenue and 4th to 6th Avenues on the Ship Bottom side, and a few on South 1st and 2nd Streets in Surf City. Water pipes run along the boulevard and the cross streets.
notes: 4th to 6th Avenues in Ship Bottom are now West and East 4th to 6th Street; Drexel Road is Drexel Avenue.
The old Ocean Avenue is not the modern South Ocean Terrace (about 200 ft bayward); not used for control.
Borough limits of Ship Bottom and Surf City drawn down 3rd Avenue / South 3rd Street.

Five parts, 100 ft, separated by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington and Surf City, 6th Av to N. 1st St, Central, Drexel Rd, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av; borough limits down 3rd Av. Part 2 (middle left): Brant Beach 52nd to 45th St. Part 3 (middle right): Surf City N. 5th and N. 6th St. Part 4 (lower left): Brant Beach 45th to 38th St, Ockanickon Hotel. Part 5 (lower right): Surf City N. 14th to N. 16th St. The old Ocean Avs of Surf City are not the modern Ocean Terraces; parts 3 and 5 rest on boulevard junctions only.

sheet-22-2.description: Second part of sheet 22, a strip between heavy lines on the left: Brant Beach from 52nd Street to 45th Street at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right. Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard runs along the top edge and Ocean Boulevard across the lower third, with a row of beach-front blocks below it cut by the dividing line. The cross streets are 52nd, 51st, 50th, 49th, 48th, 47th, 46th and 45th Streets. Blocks 7 to 22 are platted into lots, with a handful of dwellings, mostly between Ocean Boulevard and the boulevard. Water pipes run down several cross streets to Ocean Boulevard. The strip continues on the part below (45th to 38th Streets).
notes: Cross streets are now East 45th to East 52nd Street.

Five parts, 100 ft, separated by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington and Surf City, 6th Av to N. 1st St, Central, Drexel Rd, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av; borough limits down 3rd Av. Part 2 (middle left): Brant Beach 52nd to 45th St. Part 3 (middle right): Surf City N. 5th and N. 6th St. Part 4 (lower left): Brant Beach 45th to 38th St, Ockanickon Hotel. Part 5 (lower right): Surf City N. 14th to N. 16th St. The old Ocean Avs of Surf City are not the modern Ocean Terraces; parts 3 and 5 rest on boulevard junctions only.

sheet-22-3.description: Third part of sheet 22, at the middle right between heavy lines: a short stretch of Surf City around North 5th and North 6th Streets at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right. Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard runs along the top and Ocean Avenue along the bottom, with a note that the Atlantic Ocean lies 100 ft beyond. Blocks 16, 20 and 23 are platted into lots with a few dwellings and a brick store building at the boulevard and North 6th Street. A domestic-service water pipe runs along the boulevard.
notes: The old Ocean Avenue has no modern counterpart here.
Placed from one detected and one hand-picked junction on the boulevard, 272 ft apart, plus a derived point: low confidence.

Five parts, 100 ft, separated by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington and Surf City, 6th Av to N. 1st St, Central, Drexel Rd, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av; borough limits down 3rd Av. Part 2 (middle left): Brant Beach 52nd to 45th St. Part 3 (middle right): Surf City N. 5th and N. 6th St. Part 4 (lower left): Brant Beach 45th to 38th St, Ockanickon Hotel. Part 5 (lower right): Surf City N. 14th to N. 16th St. The old Ocean Avs of Surf City are not the modern Ocean Terraces; parts 3 and 5 rest on boulevard junctions only.

sheet-22-4.description: Fourth part of sheet 22, the lower left strip: Brant Beach from 45th Street to 38th Street at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right, continuing the strip above. Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard runs across the top and Ocean Boulevard across the lower part, with beach-front blocks below. The cross streets are 45th, 44th, 43rd, 42nd, 41st, 40th, 39th and 38th Streets. The Ockanickon Hotel and its club house stand at the boulevard by 45th Street, and a garage for ten cars on the boulevard between 43rd and 42nd Streets; otherwise the blocks hold scattered dwellings on platted lots. The Princeton map division stamp is printed in block 37 by 38th Street.
notes: Cross streets are now East 38th to East 45th Street.
Ockanickon Hotel at 45th Street and the boulevard.

Five parts, 100 ft, separated by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington and Surf City, 6th Av to N. 1st St, Central, Drexel Rd, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av; borough limits down 3rd Av. Part 2 (middle left): Brant Beach 52nd to 45th St. Part 3 (middle right): Surf City N. 5th and N. 6th St. Part 4 (lower left): Brant Beach 45th to 38th St, Ockanickon Hotel. Part 5 (lower right): Surf City N. 14th to N. 16th St. The old Ocean Avs of Surf City are not the modern Ocean Terraces; parts 3 and 5 rest on boulevard junctions only.

sheet-22-5.description: Fifth part of sheet 22, the lower right corner: north Surf City around North 14th, 15th and 16th Streets at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right. A strip of small lots lies above Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard, and blocks 47 and 50 run from the boulevard down to Ocean Avenue. There are a few dwellings and a brick house at the boulevard. The sheet's scale bar is printed at the bottom.
notes: North 14th to 16th Streets are now 14th to 16th Street; the boulevard here is North Long Beach Boulevard.
The old Ocean Avenue lies about 130 ft oceanward of modern Ocean Terrace; not used.
Placed from three junctions along the boulevard only (helmert): low confidence.

Five parts, 100 ft, separated by heavy lines. Part 1 (top): Ship Bottom-Beach Arlington and Surf City, 6th Av to N. 1st St, Central, Drexel Rd, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av; borough limits down 3rd Av. Part 2 (middle left): Brant Beach 52nd to 45th St. Part 3 (middle right): Surf City N. 5th and N. 6th St. Part 4 (lower left): Brant Beach 45th to 38th St, Ockanickon Hotel. Part 5 (lower right): Surf City N. 14th to N. 16th St. The old Ocean Avs of Surf City are not the modern Ocean Terraces; parts 3 and 5 rest on boulevard junctions only.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 shows the grid of Surf City from 7th Street at the left to 14th Street at the right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The numbered streets (lettered N. 7th to N. 14th) run across the sheet, crossed by Barnegat Avenue near the top, Central Avenue in the middle, and Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard in the lower third, with Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean at the bottom. The upper two thirds, between Barnegat and Central Avenues, is a regular pattern of long blocks (24 to 46) of narrow platted lots with only about twenty dwellings, scattered along 8th to 13th Streets. Building is concentrated near the boulevard and Central Avenue and in the lower rows: the Surf City Hotel between 8th and 9th Streets, a borough hall (Boro Hall) between 11th and 12th, a Roman Catholic church and a pump house with a steel water tower (domestic service) and a garage near 13th and 14th Streets, and bath houses and a pavilion along the beach at the bottom right. A 'Proposed Street' is lettered across the left of Central Avenue. A water supply line from the domestic service is shown along 6 inch pipes, and Barnegat Bay appears at the top right corner. A compass rose is at the top left, and the title oval with 'Surf City' at the right.
notes: Printed N. 7th to N. 14th St.; the modern names are North 7th to North 12th Street, then 13th Street and 14th Street (plain), and North Barnegat Avenue, North Central Avenue and North Long Beach Boulevard.

The boulevard junctions at North 7th to North 10th Street were not detected (the drawn boulevard bends there); the control rests on the Barnegat Avenue and Central Avenue rows, 14th Street's Barnegat junction was left out (4.6 m, one street edge), and the 12th Street junctions were not detected.
Domestic service water tower and pump house at 13th and 14th Streets; the scale bar reads 100 ft to one inch.
Surf City, 100 ft, one part: N. 7th to N. 14th St, Barnegat, Central, Bay Av or Long Beach Blvd, Ocean Av (not opened). Helper-configured.

sheet-24-1.description: Main part of sheet 24: High Point, officially the Borough of Harvey Cedars, at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard runs up the sheet and north points to the upper left. It covers 74th Avenue at the bottom to 83rd Street at the top, from Barnegat Bay and the Yacht Basin on the left to the proposed Ocean Avenue and the Atlantic Ocean on the right. Cross streets are 75th to 78th Streets, 79th Avenue and 80th to 83rd Streets; a short street by the water works is marked not named. Buildings include the High Point Inn near 82nd Street, the borough water works pumping station with a steel tower and reservoir on 80th Street, the High Point Volunteer Fire Company near 77th Street, the Highpoint Yacht Club with a wooden pier on the bay, and dwellings along the boulevard and 76th to 78th Streets. Most ocean-side blocks are platted lots with few houses.
notes: Cross streets are now West and East 75th to 83rd Street.
Ocean Avenue is marked proposed.
All control lies along the boulevard (helmert).

Two parts, 100 ft, turned: Long Beach Blvd runs up the sheet, north to the upper left (rotation about -20.5). Part 1: High Point (Borough of Harvey Cedars), 74th Av to 83rd St, Yacht Basin, High Point Inn, water works, fire company, Highpoint Yacht Club. Part 2: inset in the lower left corner, 74th Av to 72nd St and a Private Way, the continuation southward. Only boulevard junctions survive (helmert / anchored).

sheet-24-2.description: Inset in the lower left corner of sheet 24, outlined by a heavy line: the southern end of High Point (Harvey Cedars) from 74th Avenue to below 72nd Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left like the main map. Bay Avenue or Long Beach Boulevard runs along the left edge, 73rd Street and 72nd Street (marked not open) cross the island, and a 20 ft Private Way runs below 72nd Street; the ocean lies beyond the right edge. Blocks 562 to 564 hold a hall and a few dwellings, and the cottage Langdune stands south of 72nd Street. The inset continues the main map southward; it was drawn here for room.
notes: 72nd Street is marked 'not open'.
Langdune, a cottage south of 72nd Street.
Anchored on 73rd Street at the boulevard with the scale and rotation of part 1: low confidence.
